coverageNote: Read every current Markdown source file recursively under .memory/wiki/specs/ideation/09-rights-ownership/: the root unit plus 09.01 through 09.06. Each of the 7 units received the 3a implementer simulation, 3b Vision Rubric scoring, and 3c devil's-advocate probe across all 8 rubric dimensions (56 applicable checkpoints).

findings.claim: The root decision records omit a deadline and do not consistently record the decision each question blocks; `Deferred To` identifies a stage, not either required fact.

evidence.excerpt: Is a WeJammin split sheet enforceable or evidentiary?
Medium pending validation of exactly where detection fires (at the second assignment vs at a later title search).

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose the legal/evidentiary consent posture and the double-assignment detection trigger without a scheduled, recorded dependency resolution.
findings.failureScenario: Equivalent split consents receive incompatible verification treatment, or conflicting title assignments are detected only after downstream rights actions proceed.

findings.claim: Unresolved registry decisions are assigned an owner and target stage but lack a deadline and consistently recorded blocked decision, leaving authorization behavior without an accountable resolution point.

evidence.excerpt: its meaning is not yet written — see Q-10

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must define which actions a lone co-owner may take, duties to other owners, notification/objection behavior, and the resulting Control Summary verdict.
findings.failureScenario: A unilateral owner can be granted an invented licensing or release authority, or a valid non-exclusive path is silently unavailable with no dependable resolution deadline.

findings.claim: The unit records deferred open decisions without a deadline or consistently recorded blocked decision; its deferred producer-points/work-for-hire interaction also lacks an accountable resolution record.

evidence.excerpt: The model must scope both to a contribution, not to a person.
CX-05 remains deferred to `/ideate-discover` Step 5. It is Medium confidence.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose the contribution identity and cardinality that allow work-for-hire and producer points to be mutually exclusive per contribution while coexisting for one person.
findings.failureScenario: A person-scoped model collapses separate engineering and production work into a false either/or, misrecording ownership, fee, or royalty obligations.

findings.claim: Active chain-of-title questions have an owner and routing target but no deadline or consistently recorded decision blocked, including the scope of asserted historic-title imports.

evidence.excerpt: Does the platform accept bulk catalogue import of asserted prior history?

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide whether bulk historic-title imports exist and, if so, the authority and provenance boundary for asserted chain events.
findings.failureScenario: Established catalogues are either excluded without a product decision or imported with an invented trust posture that can be mistaken for consented title.

findings.claim: The dispute unit's unresolved terminal-state and release-policy questions lack a deadline and consistently recorded decision blocked, despite defining the operational boundary for disputed rights.

evidence.excerpt: If the platform never adjudicates, how does a dispute ever end when both parties dig in?
Does a dispute make the work unusable (release-blocked, licence-blocked) or only unpaid (escrowed)?

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose a dispute terminal path and whether disputes block continuing release/licensing or only affect payments.
findings.failureScenario: The product either permits exploitation during a rights conflict or freezes innocent owners' releases and income under an unapproved policy.

findings.claim: The AI-consent questions assign owners and future stages but omit a deadline and consistently recorded decision blocked, including whether the platform's own AI may train on user content.

evidence.excerpt: Do WeJammin's own AI features (anywhere in the platform) train on user content?

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose whether first-party AI training is permitted and whether the consent registry gates that use before any model or data pipeline is specified.
findings.failureScenario: User content can enter a first-party training pipeline without a recorded authority model, or consent controls can be built that protect only third parties.

findings.claim: Public-record decisions are routed but not given a deadline or consistently recorded decision blocked, leaving the publication boundary unresolved.

evidence.excerpt: Is the public lookup open to the internet (SEO, unauthenticated, the Jaxsta-shaped play) or gated to platform users?

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose the public projection, owner-control boundary, and authenticated versus internet-open access model.
findings.failureScenario: The lookup can expose commercially sensitive rights data or be constrained by an invented access policy that defeats the intended public-record use case.
